topic.title: Compatibility of memory-joint representation and task conditioning
topic.question: Under the frozen inputs and training protocol, does combining the committed g0 memory-joint representation with the g3 task-conditioning approach exceed both frozen source bests, especially validation four-task macro ROC-AUC 0.8303789178781177, at justified parameter and measured compute cost?
topic.hypothesis: The two committed approaches may preserve complementary information, but their shared representation ancestry may make task conditioning redundant or introduce task interference. Inherit their approaches only after implementation inspection in the next phase. Improvement over both frozen bests and matched-capacity source-replacement/factorial controls, followed by repetition, would support added utility; failure to exceed the stronger source or benefits reproduced by capacity alone would oppose it. Recent unsuccessful mean/copy variants constrain those implementations without refuting task conditioning generally. No novelty or confirmed mechanism is claimed.
